text: specify model first. just toy model illustrative purposes.
code: # Load the dataset. This dataset was taken from lavaan 6.2.1. Versions >0.7 have removed it. data("FacialBurns", package = "Lmisc") model <- " HADS ~ Age HADS ~ Sex HADS ~ TBSA TBSA ~ Age TBSA ~ Sex " fit_model <- sem(   model = model,   data = FacialBurns,   missing = "fiml" ) summary(fit_model) #> lavaan 0.7-2 ended normally after 1 iteration #>  #>   Estimator                                         ML #>   Optimization method                           NLMINB #>   Number of model parameters                         9 #>  #>   Number of observations                            77 #>   Number of missing patterns                         1 #>  #> Model Test User Model: #>                                                        #>   Test statistic                                 0.000 #>   Degrees of freedom                                 0 #>  #> Parameter Estimates: #>  #>   Standard errors                             Standard #>   Information                                 Observed #>   Observed information based on                Hessian #>  #> Regressions: #>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|) #>   HADS ~                                               #>     Age               0.043    0.055    0.779    0.436 #>     Sex               4.413    1.848    2.388    0.017 #>     TBSA              0.220    0.107    2.066    0.039 #>   TBSA ~                                               #>     Age               0.073    0.058    1.255    0.209 #>     Sex               3.088    1.945    1.588    0.112 #>  #> Intercepts: #>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|) #>    .HADS             -0.435    3.071   -0.142    0.887 #>    .TBSA              2.973    3.267    0.910    0.363 #>  #> Variances: #>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|) #>    .HADS             43.473    7.006    6.205    0.000 #>    .TBSA             49.727    8.014    6.205    0.000

title: How to use it with Lavaan
code: dag <- ggdag::dagify(   HADS ~ Age,   HADS ~ Sex,   HADS ~ TBSA,   TBSA ~ Age,   TBSA ~ Sex,   outcome = "TBSA",   coords = list(     x = c(       TBSA = 0,       HADS = 4,       Age = 2,       Sex = 2     ),     y = c(       HADS = 0,       TBSA = 0,       Age = 1,       Sex = -1     )   ),   labels = c(     # If you need to change the names, specify the labels here     HADS = "HADS",     TBSA = "TBSA",     Age = "Age",     Sex = "Sex"   ) )   tidy_dag <- ggdag::tidy_dagitty(dag)

title: How to use it with Lavaan
code: nodes <- tidy_dag$data %>%   filter(!duplicated(name)) %>%   dplyr::transmute(     node_id = name,     x = x,     y = y,     label = label   ) %>%   mutate(node_id = label)  # If you need curved paths edges <- tidy_dag$data %>%   mutate(     curvature = case_when(       name == "Sex" & to == "HADS" ~ 1,       TRUE ~ 0 # default: straight     )    ) |>    mutate(     curvature_amount = case_when(       name == "Sex" & to == "HADS" ~ 0.3,       TRUE ~ 0      )    )

title: How to use it with Lavaan
code: parameters_fit_model <- modify_parameter_estimates(   df = parameterestimates(     fit_model,     standardized = F   ),   round_digits = 2 )   temp <- data.frame(   # Extract only the regression paths   parameters_fit_model[     parameters_fit_model$op == "~",      ] )   edges <- left_join(   x = edges,   y = temp,   by = join_by(     # rhs =  right hand side = where the path starts     # lhs = left hand side = where the path ends     name == rhs,      to == lhs   ) )  # Rename and keep only what we need edges <- edges %>%   filter(!is.na(to)) %>%   transmute(     from = name,     to = to,     curvature = curvature,     curvature_amount = curvature_amount,     pvalue = pvalue,     est = est,     ci.lower = ci.lower,     ci.upper = ci.upper   )  edges <- edges |>    mutate(     hjust = case_when(       from == "Sex" & to == "HADS" ~ 0.5,       .default = 0.5     )   ) |>    mutate(     vjust = case_when(       from == "Sex" & to == "HADS" ~ 0.5,       .default = 0.5     )   ) |>    mutate(     gap = case_when(       from == "Sex" & to == "HADS" ~ -0.5,       .default = -1     )   )

title: How to use it with Lavaan
code: plot_dag(   nodes = nodes,   edges = edges,   label_size = 10,   label_size_unit = "pt",   text_size = 4,   xlim = c(-0.5, 4.4),   ylim = c(-1.5, 1.5) ) #> Warning: The text offset exceeds the curvature in one or more paths. This will result in #> displaced letters. Consider reducing the vjust or text size, or use the hjust #> parameter to move the string to a different point on the path.

title: How-to-use
text: First need build two dataframes; one containing info nodes one containing lines node dataframe must contain columns . row represents node. dataframe describes relationship aforementioned nodes. indicate start end node. curvature takes two values; 1 means line curved 0 ’s straight line. pvalue, est, ci.upper, ci.lower p-value, estimate, upper confidence interval lower confidence interval estimate. drawn top lines vjust hjust indicates vertical horizontal offset text top line gap controls gap boxes start/end straight line positive values increase length line negative values opposite. gap=0 means line start ends exact centers boxes. Default value 1. need granular control, specify values relationship. curvature_amount controls curvature curved paths. follow notation ggplot: positive values mean right-hand curve negative values left-hand curve.
code: library(Lmisc) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) nodes <- data.frame(     node_id = c("A", "C", "B", "D"),     label = c("A", "C", "B", "D"),     x = c(0, 14, 14, 0),     y = c(0, 3, 0, 3)   ) edges <- data.frame(   from = c(     "A", "C", "B", "D"   ),   to = c(     "B", "D", "C", "A"   ),   curvature = c(0, 0, 0, 0),   pvalue = c(0.1, 0.30, 0.5, 0.5),   est = c(     0.2, 0.15, -0.25, -0.3   ),   ci.lower = c(0.4, 0.1, -0.6, -0.3),   ci.upper = c(1.2, 0.9, 0.0, -0.3),   hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5),   vjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.50, 0.5),   curvature_amount = c(     0, 0, 0, 0   ) )

title: How-to-use
code: p <- plot_dag(nodes, edges, ylim = c(-0.2, 3.2), xlim = c(-0.2, 14.2), text_size = 3) print(p)

title: How-to-use
text: Imagine ’re walking along path start end:  walk D (C D) negative value (curvature_amount = -0.2), curved path left-handed. walk B C (B) positive value, path right-handed (curvature_amount = 0.2).

title: Adjust edge start and end so they touch the box border — adjust_edges_by_box
text: edges_df data frame containing edge information minimum: Character integer identifier source node Character integer identifier target node curvature Numeric indicator; 1 curved edges, 0 straight Additional columns preserved output. nodes_df data frame containing node information required columns: node_id Unique identifier matching edges$edges$x X-coordinate node center y Y-coordinate node center half_w Half-width node bounding box half_h Half-height node bounding box values typically come compute_node_boxes.

title: Adjust edge start and end so they touch the box border — adjust_edges_by_box
text: data frame columns `edges_df` plus four new columns: xstart_adj Adjusted X-coordinate edge start point ystart_adj Adjusted Y-coordinate edge start point xend_adj Adjusted X-coordinate edge end point yend_adj Adjusted Y-coordinate edge end point is_horizontal Logical flag indicating nearly-horizontal lines is_vertical Logical flag indicating nearly-vertical lines Rows reordered regular straight lines first, followed horizontal,   curved edges.

title: Adjust edge start and end so they touch the box border — adjust_edges_by_box
text: function performs several adjustments: Joins node position box dimension data edge Uses geometric intersection calculate precise edge--box connection points Applies special offsets horizontal lines (reduces overlap) Applies different offsets curved edges improve visual aesthetics critical preprocessing step rendering DAG plots, ensures arrows visually connect perimeter node boxes without penetrating . function leverages line_rect_intersection accurate intersection calculations.

title: Adjust edge start and end so they touch the box border — adjust_edges_by_box
text: **General Case**: Uses `line_rect_intersection` find line node center node center intersects perimeter node's bounding box. **Horizontal Lines**: efficiency visual consistency, applies simplified offset (0.5 * half-width) instead full intersection calculation. keeps horizontal arrows visibly separated nodes. **Curved Lines**: Applies custom offsets (quarter width, full height) ensure curved edges emerge appropriate positions node boundaries.

title: Adjust edge start and end so they touch the box border — adjust_edges_by_box
text: function requires: dplyr data manipulation (left_join, mutate, dplyr::filter, bind_rows) line_rect_intersection geometric calculations
